label: Standard of favouring: value ranking or end-realization ordering
resolution: The loss and arbitrariness bridges (MissingVerdictIsImpure, UnbackedVerdictIsImpure) measure a favouring profile against a standard, and their verdict on the disputed pair depends on which. STANDARD_OF_FAVOURING_1 (ValueStandard): the betterness ranking read as value; with it a favouring determined to end content D misses a verdict wherever betterness varies within a D-class, and the good-tracking favouring tracks it exactly. STANDARD_OF_FAVOURING_2 (EndRealizationStandard): the end-realization ordering; with it the good-tracking favouring makes an unbacked verdict (c over d at cBetter on the control carrier) and the D-directed favouring tracks it exactly. The statements 720bccc2 and a141e6a8 and the registered argument b86a2364 use sense 1 only: the parameter good is the value ranking. The D-relative form is the same Lean function applied with sense 2; it appears only in Lean-only controls (standardControls row 6, standardRelativity) and is not a corpus statement. The Lean marker ValueStandard is a declared-primitive tag, definitionally the supplied ranking: bind-check sees the tag, not the reading, and mixing the senses is not a type error (ValueStandard (EndRealizationStandard fit) reduces to EndRealizationStandard fit by rfl); the conclusion's ranking is untagged and the controls use fitOrder directly. No step passes between the senses: neither is defined from the other, and on the control carrier they differ at one verdict in genuine scenarios. Whether a single standard governs every favouring, and which, or whether each favouring is measured by the formal object of its kind of operation (so that the verdict on a root's favouring turns on whether it is a natural or a rational appetite), is the open question of docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section 'When is a restriction of content a limitation?'.
